title: Magnets and Static Electricity
seo_title: Grade 3 Magnets Worksheets: Poles, Attract and Repel, and Static Electricity
standard_text: Ask questions to determine cause and effect relationships of electric or magnetic interactions between two objects not in contact with each other.
meta_desc: Free Grade 3 science worksheets on magnets and static electricity (NGSS 3-PS2-3): north and south poles, attract and repel, magnetic materials, distance and force, and charged balloons. 100 practice questions with answers.
key_big: Magnets and static electricity can push or pull without touching.
key_sub: Like poles repel and unlike poles attract. Magnets pull iron and steel, and they pull harder when they are closer.
body_html:
How to think about it

Some forces can push or pull without touching: magnetic forces and electric forces.

  • Every magnet has a north (N) and a south (S) pole. Like poles repel; unlike poles attract.
  • Magnets attract iron and steel, but not plastic, wood, glass, paper, aluminum or copper.
  • The force is stronger when the objects are closer.
  • Static electricity: a balloon rubbed on hair can pull hair or paper bits without touching them.
Example

Two magnets have S facing S. What happens?

Like poles repel.

Answer: They push apart.

Example

Will a magnet pick up an aluminum can?

Aluminum is a metal, but not iron or steel.

Answer: No.

Common mistakes

  • Thinking magnets attract all metals. They attract iron, steel and nickel.
  • Thinking like poles attract. Like poles repel.
  • Thinking magnets and static electricity only work when touching.

faq.q: What happens when you put two magnets together?
faq.a: If unlike poles (N and S) face each other, they attract. If like poles (N and N, or S and S) face each other, they repel.
No. Magnets attract iron, steel and nickel, but not aluminum, copper, gold or silver.
It is an electric charge that builds up when some things rub together. A rubbed balloon can pull on hair or paper without touching it.

items.q: Jack puts two magnets on a table. The magnets are placed with the S pole facing the S pole. What will happen?
c: They will both spin in circles.
items.e: Like poles (S and S) repel.

items.q: What happens when two north poles face each other?
items.e: Like poles repel.

items.q: Do magnets need to touch an object to pull it?
c: No. Magnetic forces can act from a distance.
items.e: Magnets can pull through air, paper and even water.
